title: On (Normalised) Discounted Cumulative Gain as an Off-Policy Evaluation Metric for Top-$n$ Recommendation

problem.claim: Recommendation approaches require evaluation, either through simulated online experiments or offline procedures intended to approximate online outcomes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Normalised Discounted Cumulative Gain and Discounted Cumulative Gain have been widely adopted in empirical top-n recommendation studies.
Higher (n)DCG values have been used for many years to present new top-n recommendation methods as state of the art.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommendation approaches are commonly evaluated through simulated online experiments or offline procedures approximating online outcomes.
Offline evaluation metrics have been adopted from ranking metrics used in Information Retrieval.
nDCG is widely used in empirical studies, and higher values have supported state-of-the-art claims for top-n recommendation methods.
